title: erf
summary: Compute error-function values element-wise in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Uses the provider unary_erf hook for real GPU tensors and restores host fallback results to the input's owning provider when the hook is unavailable.

description: `Y = erf(X)` evaluates the Gaussian error function element-by-element for real numeric input. RunMat follows MATLAB's documented real, nonsparse surface and keeps real GPU tensors resident when the active provider supports `unary_erf`.
behaviors: `erf(X)` applies the error function element-by-element while preserving the input tensor shape.
Double inputs return double results; single tensors preserve single dtype metadata with single-rounded output values.
Integer, logical, character, complex, string, sparse, table, and timetable inputs are not part of the documented surface and produce stable `RunMat:erf:InvalidInput` errors.
Real GPU tensors stay on the input's owning provider after direct execution or host fallback; malformed provider results are rejected rather than admitted as resident values.

faqs.question: Does `erf` support complex inputs?
faqs.answer: No. MATLAB documents `erf` for real single and double arrays, and RunMat reports a typed input error for complex values instead of applying a non-MATLAB analytic continuation.

faqs.question: Why use `erfc` instead of `1 - erf(x)`?
faqs.answer: For large positive `x`, `erf(x)` is very close to 1. A complementary error function can preserve the small residual more accurately than subtracting from 1.

faqs.question: Can `erf` run on GPU arrays?
faqs.answer: Yes for real tensors. The WGPU backend evaluates `erf` on device; other providers may fall back to the host if they do not expose `unary_erf`.

gpu_residency: Yes when the active provider implements `unary_erf` for real-valued gpuArray inputs. Providers without that hook trigger a host fallback, so the computed result is returned as a host tensor rather than a resident gpuArray.
implementation_notes: CPU evaluation uses libm's `erf` for double-precision real values.
WGPU kernels use a piecewise real implementation with a power series near the origin and an asymptotic complementary-error expansion in the tails.
The builtin rejects sparse and complex inputs to match MATLAB's documented `erf` input surface.
